clue.text: Fish where there's deer and heather

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: An angler wonders which fish lives where deer roam among the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckling is a hot-smoked herring, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Hand out rough treatment where there's self-service

definitions.meaning: to batter or knock about, as wind and waves do
a meal laid out for diners to help themselves

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to strike repeatedly; the noun is a spread where guests serve themselves.

clue.text: Reticent person I claim to be close

parts.note: someone who says little is said to clam up, so a clam is a tight-lipped person
my is what I say when I claim something as mine

explanation.surface: A quiet type insists on being an intimate friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and sticky, which is the damp, muggy feel of the word.

clue.text: Settling on the illumination

definitions.meaning: to light on something is to come to rest on it, as a bird does
the lamps and lights that brighten a place

explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting on means alighting or happening upon; lighting is also the arrangement of lamps.

clue.text: Women in retreat

parts.note: reads like women falling back in battle, but describes religious sisters living apart from the world, as in a spiritual retreat

explanation.definitionFit: Members of an enclosed religious order withdraw from the world, which is a retreat in the spiritual sense.

clue.text: Academic unfortunately rejecting greeting

indicators.note: rejecting here means throwing back, so the letters of both pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate academic
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A scholar sadly snubs someone's hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns the whole run MAALAS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow of greeting used in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Weapon point upthrust to hollow in body

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

indicators.note: pushed upward, which in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tip is a point

explanation.surface: A spear point is thrust upward into a cavity in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upthrust' turns TIP into PIT under ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder joint.

clue.text: A tin hut's modified to hold this plant

parts.note: a can is a tin container

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive gives the letters of hut plus S

explanation.surface: A tin shed is altered to accommodate a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' works only on the possessive, which supplies its S; the tin is the container sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a spiny Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian column decoration.

clue.text: Massaging bulge may cause this parasite to emerge

indicators.note: working and kneading something into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rubbing a lump might make a pest crawl out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mealybug is a sap-sucking insect pest covered in white powdery wax.

clue.text: Weary, carrying pavingstones

definitions.meaning: flat stones laid as a path, collectively

explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagging means tiring; flagging is also a surface of flagstones.

clue.text: Devil in the form of a wild beast

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a la, from French, means in the style or manner of

explanation.surface: A demon takes the shape of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, an untamed animal.

clue.text: Gallivanting a danger, here?

indicators.note: roaming about pleasurably, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist asks whether roaming about this island is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' points at the place the clue describes; the question mark admits this loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation, a place one might be gallivanting in.

clue.text: Devious city men caught out creating hostility

indicators.note: crooked or winding, so the letters are taken on a roundabout path into a new order
out means removed, so the letter is struck from the words

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Shifty financiers are found out, which causes ill feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes C from CITYMEN, leaving ITYMEN for 'Devious' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is deep ill will, a state of being foes.

clue.text: Painting is put to test and shows talent

parts.note: painting is a form of art
to try is to test

explanation.surface: A picture is examined and reveals skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill, a gift or flair.

clue.text: Put in to a rich stew?

definitions.text: Put in to a rich stew?

indicators.note: to stew is to cook things together and churn them up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what to add to a hearty casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the beans are what you put in a stew, and a haricot is itself a mutton stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot beans go into casseroles, and haricot of mutton is a classic stew.

clue.text: Strange — is not at all like a Scotsman?

parts.note: un- is a prefix of negation
canny, shrewd and cautious, is a Scots word long attached to the Scots stereotype

explanation.surface: Is it odd to be nothing like a typical Scot?
explanation.definitionFit: Uncanny means eerie or weird, beyond the ordinary.

clue.text: Expressed disapproval universal for short skirt

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
U is the British film classification for universal

explanation.surface: Everyone frowned upon the miniskirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is a ballerina's short stiff skirt.

clue.text: Piece of French silver soundly designed

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: by sound, so the word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: meant means intended or designed

explanation.surface: A well-made piece of French silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' swaps MEANT for MENT, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off part.

clue.text: Little wife ran, legs twinkling, after such angry exchanges

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, little meaning shortened

indicators.note: moving quickly and flickering, so the letters dart into a new order

explanation.surface: A small wife scurries off, legs flashing, after a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twinkling' (legs moving quickly) is the anagram signal; 'after such' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrangles are noisy disputes or quarrels.

clue.text: One sails out to see them?

definitions.text: One sails out to see them?

indicators.note: out means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor heads out to sea to spot marine mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: one sails out to sea to see these animals, with 'see' punning on sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lions are marine mammals, seen by those who go out on boats.

clue.text: It's unusual to return right on time

indicators.note: to go back, so the letters run in the opposite direction
in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: It is uncommon to come back at the correct moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right on time' makes ERA then R; 'to return' turns ERAR round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom found, infrequent.

clue.text: Girl not an out-and-out Marxist?

parts.note: mild means moderate, not extreme
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Is she only a moderate communist?
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a woman's name.

clue.text: Epidemic caused by flocculus around mid- January

indicators.note: around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a plage, or flocculus, is a bright patch on the sun's surface

indicators.note: mid- picks the middle letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An outbreak of disease is caused by a solar flare in the middle of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' gives U, the middle letter of January.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread deadly outbreak of disease.

clue.text: Graze, half-seen, under crest

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below

parts.note: the brow of a hill is its crest

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: Cattle feed below the ridge, partly visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes SE, the first half of seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to feed on leaves and shoots, as grazing animals do.

clue.text: At one point, trips out with animation

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass

indicators.note: out means displaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: At one stage, outings are full of liveliness.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit means liveliness or wit.

clue.text: Tumour causing wild beast to leave herd

parts.note: a gang is a group or herd
a lion is a wild beast, here set to depart, so it follows on after the herd

explanation.surface: A growth forms that drives an animal out of its herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' is read as the beast walking off behind the group, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cyst-like swelling, typically on a tendon.

clue.text: Lowers dazzling light on pole

parts.note: glare is harsh dazzling light
S, south, is one pole

explanation.surface: Bright light shines on a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' rhymes with 'flowers' here: it means frowns or scowls, not drops.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower is to scowl, which is to stare fiercely.

clue.text: Simple, yet wise

definitions.meaning: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.walkthrough: 'yet' is a link; 'Simple' is not the opposite of wise here but a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is a simple in old herbals; a wise person is also so named.

clue.text: Ugly vowels ruined formal speech

indicators.note: spoiled, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: E and O are two vowels

explanation.surface: Ugly vowels spoiled an official address.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of praise, often at a funeral.

clue.text: Own a farm, perhaps, or a battleship

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Should you own a farm or a warship?
explanation.definitionFit: A man-of-war is an armed sailing ship of a navy.

clue.text: Small pay, at one time, for the examiner

definitions.meaning: an old British sixpence coin, a small sum
one who tries or checks something

explanation.walkthrough: A tester was an old slang name for the sixpence, a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tester was slang for a sixpence; a tester also checks things.

clue.text: Claim again when rests are disturbed

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone repeats their claim when their rest is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert is to state or insist upon something once more.
